answer: Behavioral cohort fingerprinting. Agents are clustered by transaction timing, counterparty overlap, and session rhythm; a sudden tide of near-identical profiles triggers retroactive review of the whole cluster. Attacker cost: each synthetic identity must sustain independent behavioral noise over many sessions, and one detected link exposes the ocean of coordinated accounts, forcing costly regeneration. Legitimate drift is tolerated as a slow dune of gradual change, not a cliff edge.
